admission.justification: A real design choice with two named alternatives was weighed: rebuild the dashboard's own chat surface or reuse the host's frame with the existing launcher.

alternatives.option: Reuse the host's native frame in the rail and the one existing role launcher; remove the older panel.
alternatives.reason: The host already renders the task's agents, their tabs and the message box; the dashboard adds only the selection binding and the bound launcher.

alternatives.option: Repair the older RailChat panel to show the host's agents.
alternatives.reason: It would rebuild the host's tabs, message box and navigation inside the dashboard and keep two chat surfaces for one task.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host stops exposing an embeddable frame or a control channel the dashboard can use.

alternatives.option: Build a dashboard-native chat surface over the launch records.
alternatives.reason: It duplicates the host's message box and cannot run the agents it would display.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The product decides the host's frame is no longer the chat surface of record.

consequences: The rail keeps one launcher and one frame; the removed panel's exclusive modules and the highlight direct-target branch go with it; the launch-record read becomes the panel's single discovery source.
context: Beside a document the dashboard showed its own earlier-kind chat panel (pre-Paseo terminal sessions) while the Paseo host already ran the task's agents in its own frame and tabs.
